### A1 — Reproduced defect: canonical-shortcut declaration is inaccurate

The generator declares all five semantic rivals as `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS`.
Testing those actual functions against all usable public pairs yields:

| Declared shortcut | Matching unique canonical pairs |
|---|---:|
| ignore_blockers | 2 / 5 |
| single_step_per_blocked_row | 3 / 5 |
| shift_without_bridge | 2 / 5 |
| shift_on_any_blue_row | 5 / 5 |
| always_extra_shift | 0 / 5 |

Ten stored rows containing pairs deduplicate to five unique input/output pairs
and five unique inputs. The source distinction matters: a plausible wrong
semantic rule is not a *canonical-fitting* shortcut unless it fits them all.
Only `shift_on_any_blue_row` meets that claim in this measured set.

`checks/audit-4b1c57a69862-counterexample.json` contains a public input that passes
the target validator, its actual Racket output, the `ignore_blockers` output,
canonical pair index, source/rule hashes, and exact command/cwd. All four false
claims have full counterexamples in the larger audit report. These are public
canonical inputs in the documented domain, not invented out-of-domain stress
cases. No seed is assigned to a canonical example.

Suggested fix: retain all five as semantic/lesson competitors, but declare only
the verified canonical-fitting subset as canonical shortcuts; validate such
claims at contract load time. No source changes were made here.

### No issue found in the sampled generated rule/lesson behavior

Checked 768 draws: seeds 0..31, indices 0..7, easy/medium/hard. All pass the
validator and match the independent Racket rule against the Python mirror.
The 384 overlapping four-demo/one-query windows at starts 0..3 refute all five
actual declared rivals; zero query-disagreement or lesson-hook failures appear.
All five unique canonical pairs match Racket and pass the validator. The tool
also retains observed profile counts. This is bounded clean evidence for those
behaviors, not proof of universal correctness or a training-accuracy claim.
